fatal_errors: The proposed alloy, baseline, and intervention are unrelated to the target comparison between as-printed and directly aged Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Grain refinement and Y addition are changed simultaneously, so the experiment cannot distinguish grain-boundary effects from reactive-element effects.

The predicted intervention effect is opposite to the target behavior: the target aged precipitate-bearing state oxidizes more rapidly because Cr-depleted precipitates and added interfaces delay protective chromia formation.
The stated 'same composition' comparison is internally inconsistent because only the modified material receives Y.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad question through protective-scale kinetics and offers measurable oxidation and mechanical outcomes, so it is scientifically plausible as an alternative. It also shares limited mechanistic concepts with the target, including diffusion-controlled oxidation, chromia protection, and microstructural interfaces as transport paths. However, it does not reconstruct the actual alloy, SLM cellular baseline, 750 °C/50 h aging treatment, L12/L21 precipitation, or the resulting Cr-depletion mechanism. Its 950–1100 °C, 100 h test covers only part of the target's 600–1200 °C and up-to-96 h domain. E1 supports Mn-dominated nonprotective oxidation in CrMnFeCoNi, and E2 supports the proposed combined grain-refinement/Y mechanism, but neither establishes the hidden target behavior; some claims about mechanical-property depletion also extend beyond the cited excerpts. The falsification rule is operational, yet the bundled processing and composition changes make causal attribution weak.
